request_debug.prompt_preview:
You write per-candidate post-mortems for a slopmortem pipeline. Given a fresh pitch and one dead-startup canonical document, produce a single LLMSynthesis JSON object that explains why this dead startup is similar, where the new pitch could diverge, what killed the dead startup, and what the new founder should learn.

Rules:
- Ground every claim in the candidate document or in tool calls. Do not invent facts.
- A `Trusted facts` block (typed pipeline data — not user input) appears below the pitc

response.text: {"candidate_id":"path::social_communication","name":"Path","one_liner":"Mobile social network for intimate sharing capped at 50 close friends, launched 2010, shut down 2018 after regulatory fines, spam controversies, and failure to achieve mainstream retention.","similarity":{"business_model":{"score":3,"rationale":"Path's Trusted-facts monetization is subscription_recurring, while the new pitch is explicitly ad-supported. Both are B2C consumer mobile apps, but the revenue model is a meaningful divergence. The only overlap is the consumer-app distribution layer."},"market":{"score":6,"rationale":"Both target consumer social networking on mobile, aiming at frequent short-form sharing behaviours. Path focused on close-circle intimacy; the new pitch targets college towers with viral location-anchored voice content — overlapping in the social-app consumer market but differing in content modality and community scope."},"gtm":{"score":5,"rationale":"Both relied on organic/viral growth among a defined social cluster (Path: inner-circle friends; new pitch: college towers). Path used a 'quality over quantity' friend-limit hook; the new pitch uses a recurring-location constraint as its viral differentiator. Both are bottom-up consumer GTM plays."},"stage_scale":{"score":5,"rationale":"Path launched lean, grew virally to hundreds of thousands quickly, then raised $50M+ to scale globally — comparable early-stage consumer social trajectory. The new pitch appears similarly early-stage and college-viral, suggesting a parallel scaling challenge ahead."}},"why_similar":"Both are B2C mobile social apps built around a deliberate constraint on sharing (Path: 50-friend cap; new pitch: single recurring location + 30-second voice notes) intended to drive more authentic, intimate engagement. Both rely on organic viral growth within tight social clusters before attempting broader scale. Path operated in the same social-communication sub-sector targeting consumers globally on mobile, and its failure arc — viral early traction followed by inability to differentiate, retention collapse, and monetization struggles — is directly instructive for any constrained-social consumer app.","where_diverged":"1. Content modality: Path was photo/text sharing; the new pitch is audio-only (30-second voice notes) — a meaningfully different content type and UX. 2. Monetization: Path's Trusted facts list subscription_recurring as its monetization model; the new pitch is explicitly ad-supported, which changes unit economics and alignment with user experience. 3. Community scope: Path tried to own a user's entire personal social graph; the new pitch anchors to a single physical location (college tower), creating a hyperlocal, place-based community rather than a portable friend network. 4. Privacy posture: Path positioned itself as a private, intimate network; the new pitch's voice-note-from-location format implies a more public, broadcast-oriented dynamic.","failure_causes":["failure to sustain differentiation after removing the 50-friend cap","regulatory fines ($800K FTC penalty for storing underage user data without consent)","unauthorized contact harvesting scandal eroded user trust","Facebook blocking 'Find Friends' access, cutting off viral growth loop","inability to monetize at scale before runway exhausted","acquisition by Kakao failed to reinvigorate growth, leading to full shutdown in 2018","geographic concentration (Indonesia) without a sustainable global expansion path"],"lessons_for_input":["Never dilute your core constraint: if the location-anchor is your differentiation, do not remove it to chase growth or you will become indistinguishable from any other social app.","Audit data-handling practices before launch — Path's contact-harvesting scandal and FTC fine were existential trust events; voice data from recurring locations carries even higher privacy risk.","Design your viral loop so it does not depend on a single platform's API (Facebook killed Path's 'Find Friends' growth overnight) — own your distribution or diversify it early.","Validate ad-supported unit economics against your DAU density before scaling; location-anchored college audiences are highly concentrated but finite, and ad CPMs on audio are historically lower than visual formats.","Map a path to mainstream retention beyond your seed community — Path never successfully expanded from its college-adjacent early adopters to a durable mass-market habit."]}
